span.term: A faint probe tone drives an abnormally long response latency in collicular neurons, so the probe's discharge arrives at or after the discharge evoked by the following noise burst and is absorbed into it, which produces backward masking

span.label: Only a small number of collicular units showed backward masking, so the effect rests on few cells.

span.label: **THE DISTINCTION IS PSYCHOLOGICAL AND THE ARGUMENT IS ANATOMICAL.** `From the psychological point of view TWO KINDS of auditory masking are known, that is, SIMULTANEOUS and TEMPORAL masking` - a split made by psychophysics, which this paper then tests by asking where in the cat's auditory pathway each one appears. **A behavioural taxonomy checked against anatomy**, which is the move Carlesimo2004 makes for priming thirty-three years later and mcmahon-olson2007 makes for repetition suppression
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE LOCATION IS ESTABLISHED BY AN ABSENCE:** `Quotation withheld` Nothing was found at the first relay, therefore the mechanism is above it. **A null result at one recording site doing positive work** - which only holds because the same preparation DID show forward masking there, so the absence is not a failure of the method
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **IT IS THE PHYSIOLOGY OF marcel1983's INSTRUMENT, AND NEITHER CITES THE OTHER.** marcel1983 uses backward masking to render a prime unreportable and shows that semantic access survives it; this paper, twelve years earlier and in cats, asks WHERE backward masking happens and answers `not in the cochlear nucleus`. **One paper uses the tool, the other locates it.** The corpus holds both, and the pairing is only visible because they sit side by side - the sixth such pair found tonight
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: backward masking —distinct-from→ cochlear nucleus
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **AN EDGE BUILT ON AN ABSENCE, AND THE AXIS IS DOING THE WORK.** The sentence asserts that backward masking WAS NOT DEMONSTRABLE in the cochlear nucleus - a negative finding, and `no-change` is the only value in the enforced axis vocabulary that can carry it. Weight 0.9 because `may involve central processes` is the authors' inference from that absence and their hedge is in the quote. **A reader taking the triple alone gets `these two are distinct`, which is true but loses that the distinctness IS the finding** - the note has to say so, and this is the third time tonight that `distinct-from` has been the nearest available type rather than the right one.

span.label: Forward masking weakened as the interval between the noise burst and the probe tone grew at both recording sites, but the decline was more abrupt in the inferior colliculus than in the cochlear nucleus.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Backward masking in the inferior colliculus took three forms: "on" neurons with a long latency to the probe tone (6 units), neurons inhibited by the noise burst (3 units), and "off" neurons (2 units).
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A unit produced backward masking only when its latency to the probe tone exceeded the 20 msec at which the noise burst's own response arrived, so units responding within 20 msec showed none.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The single-neuron curves relating amount of masking to masking interval followed the same trends as the published psychophysical masking data of Elliott and Pickett, although individual neurons differed from one another.
